rows.note: This is the everyday all-purpose term for the ordinary common cold, especially with runny-nose symptoms.

example.english: I think I have a cold; my nose is running all the time.
example.traditional: 我好似傷風，成日流鼻水。
example.jyutping: ngo5 hou2 ci5 soeng1 fung1 seng4 jat6 lau4 bei6 seoi2

rows.note: Use this as the broader everyday illness label when the speaker is not distinguishing a common cold from other similar respiratory illnesses.

example.english: They said they have a cold, so they are not going to work today.
example.traditional: 佢話自己感冒，今日唔返工。
example.jyutping: keoi5 waa6 zi6 gei2 gam2 mou6 gam1 jat6 m4 faan1 gung1

rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice for low temperature and for feeling cold or uncomfortable from it.

example.english: The weather is really cold today.
example.jyutping: gam1 jat6 tin1 hei3 hou2 dung3

rows.note: Use this for someone who is unfriendly, distant, or showing little warmth toward others.

example.english: They are very cold toward people.
example.jyutping: keoi5 deoi3 jan4 hou2 laang5 daam6

rows.note: Use this when someone seems heartless, ruthless, or lacking compassion.

example.english: They treated that child like that; they’re really cold.
example.traditional: 佢咁樣對個細路，真係好冷血。
example.jyutping: keoi5 gam3 joeng6 deoi3 go3 sai3 lou6 zan1 hai6 hou2 laang5 hyut3

rows.note: Use this colloquial word when “cold” means stylish, impressive, or cool.

example.jyutping: ni1 tou3 saam1 hou2 jing4 wo3

rows.note: Use this for a measured or reported condition of low temperature, such as in weather reports, rather than for the feeling of being cold.

example.english: The Observatory says it will be cold tomorrow morning, with low temperatures.
example.traditional: 天文台話聽日清晨會出現低溫。
example.jyutping: tin1 man4 toi4 waa6 ting1 jat6 cing1 san4 wui5 ceot1 jin6 dai1 wan1
